title: Investigating the Effectiveness of ChatGPT for Providing Personalized Learning Experience: A Case Study
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT can support personalized learning in data science education, specifically for a deep learning lesson. The authors ask whether ChatGPT can improve student engagement, participation, and learning outcomes compared with traditional instruction, and whether students perceive the ChatGPT-supported experience positively.

The intervention was a case study using the 5Es instructional model (engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate) with ChatGPT acting as a virtual co-teacher. The study compared an experimental group that learned with ChatGPT against a control group that received standard teacher-led instruction. Data came from quiz scores and qualitative observations of student interaction and engagement.

The participants were 20 university students enrolled in an Internet of Things class at Qassim University in Saudi Arabia, with the lesson focused on deep learning concepts such as forward propagation, activation functions, convolutional neural networks, and network architecture. The authors report that the ChatGPT-supported group showed positive engagement and learning outcomes, and students generally perceived the experience favorably. However, they also note that ChatGPT sometimes produced incorrect evaluations or repeated/omitted steps, so teacher supervision remained necessary.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a small mixed-methods case study with a 10/10 experimental-control comparison and qualitative observations, but it is not a randomized controlled trial and provides limited methodological detail and no effect sizes. The evidence is useful but has clear credibility and generalizability limitations.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests modest positive impacts on student engagement and conceptual understanding, but the sample is very small and effects are not quantified. Without effect sizes or stronger design controls, the practical impact remains unclear beyond this pilot context.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as a virtual co-teacher to deliver personalized deep-learning instruction, answer student questions, provide tailored explanations/examples, and guide learners through the 5E instructional model with an automated evaluation quiz.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that students using ChatGPT within the 5E model showed improved understanding of deep learning concepts on a multiple-choice quiz, with several students answering all items correctly. The study is a small case study (n=20; 10 experimental, 10 control) and does not report effect sizes or confidence intervals, but the experimental group was described as performing better than the traditional-instruction control group on concept comprehension.
finding.measure: Multiple-choice quiz on deep learning concepts (forward propagation, activation functions, convolutional neural networks, network architecture)

finding.finding_summary: The authors report higher student engagement, participation, and a more positive perceived learning experience when ChatGPT was used as a personalized virtual co-teacher. Evidence is qualitative and based on observations plus learner perceptions rather than a validated engagement scale; no effect size is reported.
finding.measure: Qualitative observations of engagement/participation and students' perceived personalized learning experience
